recommendation_1: Reduce the hidden dimension in the first linear layer from 128 to 32 to drastically decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: The current model uses a 784x128 linear layer which significantly increases parameter count; reducing mid_dim to 32 will lower both RAM usage and energy consumption while maintaining acceptable performance.
recommendation_4: Switch to Bfloat16 Autocast for training and inference operations on CPU to maintain numerical precision while reducing memory usage and improving throughput.
rationale_4: Using bf16 autocast allows efficient computation without sacrificing accuracy, particularly useful for low-power devices and large-scale distributed training scenarios.
recommendation_5: Remove the ReLU activation function and dropout layer introduced in E1 to simplify the architecture and reduce computational overhead.
rationale_5: While ReLU and dropout improve generalization, they introduce additional computations that increase energy consumption and memory usage—removing them improves efficiency at minimal performance cost given the simplicity of MNIST.
